AI-Assisted (Neurosymbolic) Program Analysis

My PhD research is on AI-assisted, or neurosymbolic, program analysis — combining machine learning with traditional static analysis for binary reverse engineering. It grew out of five years as a Research Scientist at BARC, where hands-on systems-security work made me want better tools for understanding compiled code at scale.

Projects

DISA

A transformer-based disassembly framework that recovers code layout and memory block boundaries on stripped binaries, feeding downstream CFG recovery.

Skills: static disassembly, transformer models, CFG recovery

iResolveX (under review, NDSS)

A multi-stage pipeline combining high-recall indirect-call target supersets with ML-guided re-ranking, producing p-IndirectCFG.

Skills: static/binary analysis, ML-guided ranking, indirect-call resolution

CAIR (targeting ASIACCS 2027)

A GNN-based, pluggable indirect-call refinement approach using Structured Call Refinement Graphs (SCRGs).

Skills: graph neural networks, SCRG construction, benchmarking on SPEC CPU

Agentic Fuzzing for Indirect-Call Ground Truth

An AFL++-based agentic fuzzer built to establish complete ground truth for indirect-call pairs via a residual-risk framing.

Skills: fuzzer internals (AFL++), SMT-based proof, agentic systems, static/dynamic analysis

ACaM — Agent Capability Model (IBM Research)

A static analysis pipeline combining program analysis with LLM semantic-lifting to detect threats in LLM agent pipelines (LangChain/LangGraph, extending to CrewAI/AutoGen) — exfiltration chains, prompt injection, policy violations, LLM-poisoning-triggered exfiltration, and covert channels. Also covers information-flow/taint propagation across multi-agent pipelines, vulnerability scanning of deployed agentic systems, LLM-generated fuzzing grammars, and supply-chain attacks via description–implementation divergence (DID).

Skills: static analysis, LLM integration, LangChain/LangGraph internals, taint/information-flow analysis, vulnerability scanning, fuzzing grammar generation, supply chain security, threat modeling
